discovered-from:AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO

# Problem

When auditing a parent/epic whose children have stored audits, the audit runner's parent-first flow (SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F) can block the parent on child verdicts that were never actually produced.

## Root cause

1. A child's audit freshness fingerprint (`_compute_content_fingerprint`) includes the git HEAD sha. Any new commit on `dev` (even unrelated) invalidates every child's stored audit, so `_child_content_changed` returns True for all children.
2. In the default in-main-slot mode (`child_in_main_slot=True`, SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE), the child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis run are emitted as `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking agent session and are left `partial` ("pending main-session review").
3. When the runner is launched non-interactively (e.g. by a downtime worker / shell subprocess), no session services that work, so every child's `ac_results` stay `partial`. `_build_issue_json` includes child AC verdicts in `all_ac_acceptable`, so the parent is reported "Ready to close: No" even though all of the parent's own ACs are met/adjusted.
4. The runner's terminal lifecycle then demotes the parent and children to `open`/`plan_complete`.

## Observed

During AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO (Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic into a shared core scene base class), the parent's own ACs were all met/adjusted (AC8 met via `--green-run HEAD`) and the full suite was green (75 files / 1545 tests), yet the parent audit returned "No" solely because all eight children were re-screened in-main-slot and left pending. Running with `--no-child-in-main-slot` instead hit intermittent local-proxy stalls (child screens timing out at the 600 s `--child-screen-timeout` → `partial`).

## Impact

- A passing parent audit cannot be recorded for an epic whose children were previously audited, whenever HEAD has advanced, in a non-interactive audit run.
- The parent/children statuses are demoted as a side effect of the "No" restore path.

## Suggested directions (not prescriptive)

- Make the child freshness fingerprint independent of the global HEAD sha, or scope it to the child's own key files/commits, so unrelated HEAD movement does not force a full child re-audit.
- In in-main-slot mode, treat non-serviced child verdicts as "not assessed" (inherit parent pass or mark reusable) rather than blocking the parent, or auto-fall-back to the separate-process path with retry.
- Surface a clear diagnostic distinguishing "child partial because unserviced in-main-slot" from a genuine not-ready child.
data.title: Audit: parent-first flow re-audits stale children and blocks on unserviced in-main-slot verdicts

data.description:
Saving ship (or enemy) config from the gym overwrites `src/data/ship-config.csv` with only the header row + data row, dropping the `#` comment block that documents every column, enum values, and how to add entries.

**Why it matters:** the committed CSVs are documented as the "single, human-editable source of truth" (README "Configuration (CSV)"). After the first gym save, the human-readable column documentation is lost, making the file harder to hand-edit.

**Reproduction:** open the Player gym, change any value, click Save. Inspect `src/data/ship-config.csv` — the leading `#` comment lines are gone (see the `M src/data/ship-config.csv` diff on the working tree).

**Suggested approach:** have the dev-server plugin preserve the original comment prefix when rewriting the file, or move the column documentation out of the CSV (e.g. README/schema) so it is not destroyed by writes.

Discovered-from:AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V
data.title: Gym config save strips the CSV comment header block

# Test — PlayScene spawner integration tests

- **Type:** task
- **Priority:** medium
- **Parent:** AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123

## Summary

Add integration tests to `PlayScene.test.ts` covering the asteroid spawner in the scene context.

## Test Scenarios

### Spawn timing
1. First asteroid spawns within the first 10% of the wave timer.
2. Second asteroid spawns around 50% of the wave timer.
3. For waves with count=4, spawns are spread across the wave.

### Offscreen positions
4. Spawned asteroids are fully outside the viewport at spawn time.
5. Asteroids drift inward into the playfield (verified by checking velocity direction).

### Boss exclusion
6. No asteroids are spawned during the boss encounter.
7. `planAsteroidSpawns()` clears pending spawns when boss is active.

### Dynamic registration
8. Spawned asteroids are registered with WaveManager (`registerDynamicSpawn`).
9. The wave alive count includes spawned asteroids.

### Pause / transition exclusion
10. No asteroids spawn while `transitionTimer > 0`.
11. No asteroids spawn when the scene is paused.

### Determinism
12. Same `rng` seed produces the same spawn events across runs.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — add test suite for asteroid spawner integration

## Acceptance Criteria

- Integration tests exist in `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` for the asteroid spawner.
- Tests cover spawn timing driven by the public `tick(dt)`.
- Tests cover offscreen spawn positions and inward drift.
- Tests cover boss-encounter exclusion and pause/transition exclusion.
- Tests cover dynamic-spawn registration with `WaveManager`.
- Tests cover determinism with an injected RNG.
- All PlayScene tests pass.
data.title: Test — PlayScene spawner integration tests

question: Intake paused — producer input required before the brief can be finalised.

The seed description is directionally clear but contains a factual error and three genuine design decisions that materially change scope and contradict the draft AC2 ("behaviour unchanged"). I cannot finalise the acceptance criteria without answers, so the item is left at `stage: idea` and flagged for producer review.

## Evidence gathered

Shared combat core already exists:

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — abstract class defining the eight template methods (`_handleCollisions`, `_hitPlayer`, `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop`, `_spawnPlayerExplosion`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_handleTeleport`, `_readPlayerInput`).
- Already re-based: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`.
- Duplicate-body guard: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (`definesMethod()`, regex over source). It is deliberately scoped to the three re-based files and its own comment notes the standalone gyms "predate the shared core and are out of scope" and "a repo-wide scan would flag them".

Actual duplication in the three standalone gyms (verified by `grep -nE '^\s+.*_(autoFire|collectDrop|clearEnemyBullets|handleTeleport|hitPlayer)\s*\('`):

| File | Methods defined | Line refs |
|---|---|---|
| `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` | `_autoFire`, `_collectDrop` | 233, 418 |
| `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` | `_collectDrop`, `_clearEnemyBullets`, `_handleTeleport`, `_hitPlayer` | 423, 471, 538, 647 |
| `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` | `_collectDrop` | 282 |

## Conflicts with the seed description

1. **`_autoFire` is not defined in `GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`** (grep returns nothing). The description lists it as one of five methods there; the real duplication set is 7 method usages across the three files (2 + 4 + 1), not 8.
2. **Invulnerability window differs.** `GymPowerUpsCombat` uses `COMBAT_HIT_INVULNERABLE_DURATION = 0.8 s` (`src/core/constants.ts:179`); the shared `applyPlayerHit` uses `PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE = 1.5 s` (`src/core/constants.ts:158`). Adopting the shared path changes the gym's post-hit feel.
3. **Teleport ↑/↓ differs.** `GymPowerUpsCombat._handleTeleport` effectively reacts only to `S` (it computes the ↓ state then discards it via `if (!justDown) return;`); the shared `_handleTeleport` reacts to both `S` and `↓`. Aligning is a behaviour change (a likely bug fix, but a change).
4. **`GymWeapons` has no `EffectsRegistry`**, yet `CombatScene` declares `abstract getEffectsRegistry()` and uses it in `_collectDrop`/`triggerTeleport`. `GymWeapons` also maintains its own `bullets` array (not the base `playerBullets`) and a `_playShootCue` seam (the base equivalent is `onWeaponFired`).
5. **Input duplication is a fourth shared method.** All three gyms define private `_readInput` with logic identical to the base `_readPlayerInput`; the seed's "eight methods" does not mention it.

## Round 1 — blocking questions

**Q1 — Architecture.** How should the three standalone gyms consume the shared core?
- A) Extend `CombatScene` directly in all three (pull in the full combat/collision/teleport surface; give `GymWeapons` an `EffectsRegistry`).
- B) Introduce a narrower shared mixin/base (drop collection + auto-fire + input) and have `CombatScene` compose with it too.
- C) Hybrid: `GymPowerUpsCombat` extends `CombatScene` (it is genuinely combat-coupled); `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` use the narrower mixin (both are threat-free).

**Recommended:** C — only `GymPowerUpsCombat` is combat-coupled; forcing the two threat-free gyms to inherit an unused collision/teleport surface and an `EffectsRegistry` adds risk without exercising any extra shared combat code.

**Q2 — How strict is "behaviour unchanged"?** When a shared method differs from a gym's local behaviour (invuln 1.5 s vs 0.8 s in `GymPowerUpsCombat`; `S`+`↓` vs `S`-only teleport), do we:
- A) Adopt the shared behaviour as-is and accept the two changes (documenting the teleport `↓` as a deliberate fix);
- B) Preserve each quirk via new/extended hooks (e.g. add a `getInvulnerabilityDuration()` hook to `CombatScene`, default 1.5 s, overridden to 0.8 s in the gym); or
- C) Allow a local override method in the gym, accepting some residual divergence?

**Recommended:** B — keeps observable behaviour unchanged (AC2) while the hit *logic* still flows through one shared path; the duration constant becomes a single overridable hook. Teleport `↓` should still adopt the shared behaviour (A for that part) as it matches GDD §2.3 (`S/↓`) and fixes an apparent bug.

**Q3 — AC scope / wording.** Confirm the target is all eight shared-core method names, checked repo-wide, for every production scene file (including the three standalone gyms), and that `_readInput` should be unified onto the base `_readPlayerInput`. Also confirm the corrected duplication set (7 usages; no `_autoFire` in `GymPowerUpsCombat`).

**Recommended:** Yes — state ACs as: (1) none of the three standalone gyms define any of the eight shared method names; (2) no repo production file other than `CombatScene.ts` defines them (extend the existing guard to a repo-wide scan); (3) `_readInput` copies removed in favour of `_readPlayerInput`.

## Secondary confirmations (non-blocking if recommendations accepted)

- AC3's "repo-wide duplicate-body check": the only existing mechanism is `definesMethod()` inside `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`; confirm it should be broadened (or extracted to a shared test helper) rather than a new script.
- `GymWeapons` bullet ownership: if Q1 is C, the mixin should own the bullet list and expose the same `onWeaponFired` seam currently expressed as `_playShootCue`, so the class keeps its public `getBullets()`/`advanceBullets()` test seams.

Until these are answered the brief cannot be finalised and the stage is left at `idea`.
